item.title: Hotter seas, vanishing kelp, booming octopus: How Europe's marine life is changing
item.description: European waters have recorded their hottest summer, with rising temperatures affecting marine habitats and species. The Bay of Biscay experienced a significant temperature rise, with marine heatwaves extending throughout the season. Kelp forests in northern Spain have sharply declined, impacting local marine ecosystems. Additionally, octopus populations are surging in southern England, affecting traditional fishing yields. Non-native species are also expanding into the Mediterranean, altering local food chains and competitive dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Aryan Singh

item.title: In 1993, a project set out to reconnect wildlife habitat from Yellowstone to Canada's Yukon
item.description: The Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative is proudly nominated for Prince William's Earthshot Prize in 2026. This groundbreaking effort aims to reinstate a vital 3,400-kilometre wildlife corridor through the majestic Rocky Mountains. Achieving over 200 wildlife crossings and safeguarding around 24 million hectares, Indigenous involvement is key to strengthening conservation practices here. Looking forward, the initiative hopes to secure an extra 20 million hectares by 2030.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California acquired 640 acres near Pioneertown for western Joshua tree conservation
item.description: California state officials secured 640 acres of desert land near Pioneertown for western Joshua tree conservation. Researchers identified this land as suitable for the species despite climate change. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife completed the acquisition with funds from the Western Joshua Tree Conservation Fund. Collaboration with Native American tribes is planned for long-term stewardship of the property.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A $45 million San Francisco mansion once owned by Larry Ellison kept its new buyer secret for a year
item.description: Private equity mogul Chuck Esserman has made headlines by purchasing a lavish mansion in San Francisco for $45 million, making it the most expensive home sale in the city for 2025. Formerly owned by Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, who bought it for just $3.9 million 37 years ago, the estate boasts stunning renovations and breathtaking views of the Golden Gate Bridge, reflecting its rich legacy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Shake the prisons’: Hamas warned Israel before October 7 attack, says ex-defence minister Gallant
item.description: Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar reportedly sent a warning to Israel before the October 7 attack. Former defence minister Yoav Gallant stated that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu received international alerts about this threat. Gallant expressed that such warnings should have been prioritized as critical security issues. He claimed that Netanyahu excluded senior security officials from crucial discussions during the conflict.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: An 8,000-acre South Carolina forest was bought for conservation after drawing developer interest
item.description: Georgetown County School Board voted in favor of state plans to acquire two large land parcels for conservation. These lands would contribute to the creation of Carvers Bay State Forest and protect Arcadia East. The Board Member emphasized the importance of preserving natural spaces amid residential growth in the region. Conservation efforts received backing from local organizations and government councils expressing commitment to environmental protection.

item.title: 3 killed, 4 injured after fight erupts into gunfire at Detroit strip club in US
item.description: Three individuals lost their lives while four others sustained injuries in a shooting at a Detroit strip club. The confrontation, which occurred early on Sunday morning, stemmed from an argument between several patrons. Detroit Police Chief Todd Bettison confirmed that the three deceased victims were all men. Authorities are actively investigating the case and have received multiple complaints about the venue this year.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Nepal battered by severe rain: 21 dead, 5 missing as floods, landslides worsen
item.description: In Nepal, heavy rainfall has caused devastating floods and landslides, resulting in 21 lives lost and extensive damage. Authorities have evacuated around 3,000 residents from perilous areas to guarantee their safety. This deluge follows the earlier Bhotekoshi floods, which had a death toll of over 1,400. As rescue efforts continue, landslides have disrupted operations in several districts, and tourists in vulnerable areas are being advised to take precautions.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Louisiana neighbors' land fight over 70 feet ends with $15K damages after dead cow appears
item.description: In a prolonged conflict stemming from years of camaraderie, two families in Louisiana found themselves locked in a bitter legal battle regarding their property lines. The Colvins asserted ownership over a disputed 70-foot timberland strip, triggering rising tensions. Ultimately, the court sided with the Joneses, affirming the original boundary marked by an aged fence while ordering the Colvins to halt disruptive actions and compensate for damages.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US rejects Iran's claim of capturing underwater drone, calls move 'desperate'
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has reported the capture of a US underwater drone in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. In response, the US military dismissed this assertion, clarifying that the drone in question had experienced a malfunction prior to any claims from Iran. This development follows Iran's earlier announcement regarding another US military drone capture.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Charles Baker started garage business for his son in 1980; it has helped 12,500 plus workers
item.description: Charles P. Baker III, who died at 101, co-founded Baker Industries with his wife Louise in 1980 after their son struggled to find suitable work. What began as a two-person garage business grew into a workforce development nonprofit that has hired, trained and mentored more than 12,500 people who faced barriers to employment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Yellowstone rangers remove 20,100 pieces of trash from geothermal areas in 2026
item.description: Yellowstone rangers removed more than 20,100 pieces of trash from geothermal areas in 2026, along with over 5,000 rocks and sticks and 280 visitor hats. Staff also collected coins worth more than $18. Among the unusual finds were AirPods, golf tees, an inhaler, Invisalign retainers, fake nails and children’s toys.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pennsylvania teacher’s $5,000 donation helps turn China’s Maowusu desert into a forest of 50,000 trees
item.description: Pennsylvania teacher Ronald Sakolsky reunited with Chinese farmer Yin Yuzhen 26 years after donating $5,000 to support her tree-planting efforts in Inner Mongolia. His contribution helped Yin expand her work in the Maowusu Desert, which has since become a forest of around 50,000 trees, turning their friendship into an enduring environmental story.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2020, a New Jersey man lost his job and began mowing lawns for free; six years later...
item.description: After losing his job, Brian Schwartz founded a remarkable volunteer initiative named I Want To Mow Your Lawn. This program offers complimentary lawn care services to seniors, veterans, and others in need. Through a digital platform, volunteers across all 50 states now connect with those requiring assistance, resulting in a thriving community of over 2,000 compassionate participants who collectively enhance the spirit of service and support nationwide.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: $888 million for ads: US Republicans ramp up sends to defend 39 House seats once deemed 'safe'
item.description: Republicans are investing significantly in House races previously deemed secure as they confront emerging electoral challenges. Spending has surged to $888 million in advertising compared to $666 million by Democrats. Economic pressures are impacting traditionally Republican districts and may influence voter sentiments. Republican strategists are concerned about potential losses and are campaigning vigorously. Maintaining their House majority is now a priority for GOP leaders ahead of the elections.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan
